images.prompt: Photorealistic macro photograph of a handcrafted miniature tabletop diorama. A single frosted acrylic token about the size of a coin sits at the centre of a pale neutral tabletop, softly glowing at its milky rim. An acid-lime ring set inside the frosted disc marks it as the conversion everyone wants credit for. Two slim braided graphite cords are tied to small eyelets on opposite sides of the token and run out left and right to two small graphite capstan winches bolted to the tabletop, each with a turned handle and a brushed drum. The cords are only lightly taut. Behind, a small ivory card ledger sits folded and square. Fine fibres fray at the cord ends, and a little dust lies around the winch bases. Wide 16:9 landscape frame. The hero object sits slightly left of centre on the lower third, with the related objects extending to the right so the workflow reads left to right. Clean, generous negative space above. Shot as a real physical model, not a 3D render. Materials are limited and tactile: heavyweight ivory cotton paper and card with visible fibres, soft folds and slightly deckled edges; matte, bead-blasted graphite metal with fine machining lines, chamfered edges and tiny hex fasteners; frosted acrylic with milky edges and a soft internal glow; sandblasted frosted glass. Surfaces carry believable imperfections: fine dust, paper grain, hairline creases, light scuffs on metal. Every object has convincing miniature scale and weight and rests firmly on its surface. Colour palette is restrained and nearly monochrome: white #FFFFFF, warm ivory, pale neutral #F3F5F2, soft grey-green #DCE1DA, muted graphite #626A64 and deep graphite #191D1B. Acid lime #D0F344 appears only on the lime element named in the scene, as the single signal colour, with olive #718D0B on its shadowed sides. Nothing else is lime or saturated; no red, orange or blue accents. Lighting: one large soft key light from the upper left at about 45 degrees, like diffused north-window daylight, with a gentle white bounce fill from the right; soft grounded contact shadows fall to the lower right. Camera: 100mm macro lens at f/4, eye level with the tabletop, three-quarter view. The hero object is tack sharp and the background melts into smooth, creamy blur on a seamless pale neutral sweep. Mood: calm, precise, orderly and quietly premium, like high-end editorial product photography. Strictly no people, figures, faces, hands or silhouettes. No readable text, letters, numbers, clock digits, logos, signage or user-interface graphics anywhere. No holograms, floating screens, robots with faces, dense cable tangles, carnival or circus elements, cartoon or plastic CGI look, oversaturated colour, lens flare or heavy vignette.

Photorealistic macro photograph of a handcrafted miniature tabletop diorama, captured mid-disaster. The same token is now at the centre of a starburst of cords. Six or seven more graphite capstan winches have been bolted around it, each cranked tight, and every cord is strained taut in a different direction. The frosted disc has cracked across, and the lime ring is bending and splitting, a sliver frozen mid-air as it snaps free. Two winches are tearing out of the tabletop, their bolts lifting. The ivory ledger behind has been dragged open by a stray cord and torn along its fold. Fine acrylic chips and cord fibres are suspended in the air around the token, and every taut line points back to the cracked centre. Wide 16:9 landscape frame, same layout and angle as the calm version of this scene. The hero object stays slightly left of centre, and the spread of the disaster runs to the right and toward the camera so its path can be traced back to the source. Shot as a real physical model, not a 3D render. Surfaces carry believable imperfections: fine dust, paper grain, hairline creases, light scuffs on metal. Every object has convincing miniature scale and weight and rests firmly on its surface. Nothing else is lime or saturated; no red, orange or blue accents. Lighting: the same soft upper-left key and right-side bounce fill as a calm studio setup, unchanged, so the disorder reads as physical and real rather than theatrical. Airborne paper, grains and fragments catch the key light with crisp edge highlights. Camera: 85mm lens at f/5.6, same three-quarter tabletop angle, fast shutter freezing everything mid-air. Photorealistic photograph of a vast handcrafted miniature landscape diorama. A vast cracked dry lakebed stretches to a hazy horizon, its pale clay surface split into curling plates. In the centre lies the building-sized frosted token, shattered into wedge-shaped slabs, each still tethered by snapped, sun-bleached graphite cords that lie in long frayed lines radiating across the lakebed toward giant rusted capstan winches half sunk at its edges. The torn ivory ledger is a weathered fold of card rising from the clay like a tent. In the midground, a slim graphite balance rig on three spindly legs stands over the shards, its lime ledger scale lifting the wedge fragments one by one and setting them onto clearly divided graphite trays, fitting each piece to the channel that earned it. Wide 16:9 panoramic frame. The main ruin anchors the left or centre foreground, terrain rolls back to a distant horizon on the upper third, and the lime recovery rig sits in the right midground. Surfaces carry believable imperfections: fine dust, paper grain, hairline creases, light scuffs on metal. Every object has convincing miniature scale and weight and rests firmly on its surface.
